title: Lab document v3 — pedagogy, electronics, content, safety and evidence
description: The structure of one finished lab. Five co-equal blocks: pedagogy (how it teaches), sequence (the 5E lesson), electronics (the electrical model — spec, quantities, circuit, behaviour, ratings, failure modes, calculations, measurements), content (physical assembly), safety (what must be verified). v2 specified the lesson but modelled no electronics; that block is the domain spine and is now required.

title.description: The component is the title. A problem is an application, never the organising principle.

component_job_sentence.description: The component's main job in one sentence a nine-year-old can repeat.

pedagogy.description: How this lab teaches. Every field here implements a named, evidence-based method; see meta_prompt/pedagogy.v1.md.

learning_objectives.description: Bloom's revised taxonomy. Each objective states an observable behaviour and pairs with a child-facing success criterion (Black & Wiliam). At least one objective must reach 'understand' or higher — identification alone is not a lab.

statement.description: Begins with an observable verb: identify, describe, predict, explain, compare, trace, test.

success_criterion.description: Child-facing, first person: 'I can …'. The child must be able to judge this themselves.

prior_knowledge.description: What the lab assumes, stated rather than implied. Undeclared prior knowledge is a pedagogy-QA rejection.

assumed_ideas.description: Every idea taken as already known. Empty only for L01.

retrieval_prompt.description: Retrieval practice (Roediger & Karpicke): the child recalls a prior idea from memory before new material is introduced. Not a re-read, a recall.

misconceptions.description: Conceptual change (Posner et al.): a wrong idea must be surfaced and confronted with evidence, not merely avoided. At least one — every electronics topic has a common alternative conception.

confronted_by.description: The specific observation, comparison or step in this lab that makes the wrong idea untenable.

vocabulary.description: Cognitive load theory (Sweller): at most two new technical terms per lab, each defined at first use, beside its first useful visual.

scaffolding.description: Guided participation with planned fading (Wood, Bruner & Ross; Vygotsky). The adult's role must shrink across the workbook, not stay constant.

fading_note.description: What the child now does alone that an adult did in an earlier lab.

cognitive_load.description: Segmenting and worked-example effect (Mayer; Sweller). Concrete object and action before abstract symbol (CRA sequence).

segments.description: The lab broken into learner-paced chunks. More than six is overload for this age.

concrete_before_abstract.description: The physical object or action the child meets before any schematic symbol or abstract term.

worked_example.description: Optional. A fully worked instance shown before the child attempts one alone.

sequence.description: The 5E instructional model (Bybee/BSCS). Order is fixed; the child reads it in this order.

engage.description: 5E-1. Surface curiosity and elicit what the child already thinks. Not a summary of what is coming.

eliciting_question.description: Draws out the child's existing idea — including a wrong one — before teaching begins.

explore.description: 5E-2. Hands-on, structured as Predict-Observe-Explain (White & Gunstone). The prediction is committed before the observation, or the cycle does nothing.

steps.description: One physical action per numbered step.

not_yet_outcome.description: A safe 'not yet' result is a legitimate outcome, not a failure. Troubleshooting always starts with power off.

explain.description: 5E-3. Mechanism, after the child has evidence to attach it to. Observation and deeper mechanism must be distinguishable.

what_you_saw.description: The observable level, in the child's own terms.

why_it_happened.description: The mechanism level. Scientifically honest, no metaphor-only explanation, using only vocabulary already introduced.

self_explanation_prompt.description: Self-explanation effect (Chi): the child restates the mechanism in their own words before moving on.

elaborate.description: 5E-4. Transfer. Near transfer applies the idea in a familiar setting; far transfer shows it in the world beyond the kit.

near_transfer.description: Applications of this component, changing one variable or adding one tightly scoped part at a time.

far_transfer.description: Two or three real-world uses. Applications of the component, never replacement lab themes.

evaluate.description: 5E-5. Formative assessment (Black & Wiliam). The child can tell whether they succeeded without being told.

success_criteria_checklist.description: Mirrors the 'I can …' criteria from learning_objectives, as a child-tickable list.

hinge_question.description: One question whose answer reveals whether the key idea landed or a misconception survived.

next_lab_link.description: Optional. How this lab's idea is picked up next — spacing the practice rather than closing the topic.

electronics.description: The electrical model of the lab. This is the domain spine: what the component IS electrically, what it does to a circuit, what may be measured, and what must never be exceeded. Every value is datasheet- or measurement-backed; a guessed electrical value is a failed gate.

component_spec.description: What the part is, from primary sources.

designator_prefix.description: R, C, D, Q, U, LS, M …

parameters.description: Datasheet parameters that matter in this lab — forward voltage, max current, resistance tolerance, logic thresholds, coil voltage, etc. Each carries its measurement condition and its source.

condition.description: The test condition the value holds under, e.g. 'at If = 20 mA, 25 C'.

source.description: Datasheet or official listing. Not a recollection.

quantities_taught.description: Which electrical quantities this lab actually teaches, and how far. 'observe' is qualitative, 'measure' puts a meter on it, 'calculate' means the child or adult computes a value.

child_facing_meaning.description: How this quantity is described to a nine-year-old without falsifying it.

circuit.description: The machine-readable circuit. Prose steps, connection tables, maps and schematics are all generated from this — never written independently.

name.description: Named net, e.g. P_PLUS, P_MINUS, N1. Rail colour is never an electrical identity.

sequence.description: Power-on and power-off order where it matters.

introduced_after_physical.description: CRA sequence: the child meets the object before the symbol. Always true.

calculations.description: Every electrical value that is derived rather than measured. Current limiting is mandatory wherever current flows through a rated part.

margin_to_rating.description: How far the result sits below the absolute maximum, and against which rating. 'None' is not an acceptable answer for a powered lab.

measurements.description: What is actually measured, with the meter set up explicitly. An expected value without a tolerance is not a measurement.

lead_socket.description: Which socket the red lead occupies — the current range is a different socket, and getting it wrong is how meters and supplies die.

must_stay_below.description: The rating this reading must not exceed, where one applies.

behaviour.description: How the component responds electrically — the thing the lab is actually teaching. Two levels, kept distinct so the child's version is a simplification and never a falsehood.

child_level.description: Observable cause and effect, in the child's terms.

adult_level.description: The correct electrical account — I-V relationship, threshold, timing, logic behaviour.

simplification_check.description: What the child version leaves out, and confirmation that it does not make the child version wrong. Electronics QA rejects false simplification.

ratings_and_limits.description: Absolute maxima that must never be exceeded. Fail closed: a missing rating blocks the lab.

failure_modes.description: What breaks the part or the circuit, and what in this lab prevents it. Teaching a component without teaching how it dies leaves the child to find out.

content.description: The technical spine. Every field here is generated from verified circuit data, never from prose or from a generated image.

orientation_cue.description: The polarity or orientation cue, or an explicit statement that the part has none.

build_map.description: The authority for physical assembly, deterministically rendered, never generated by ImageGen. A component lab carries a breadboard map; a foundation lab carries an unpowered path map.

troubleshooting.description: Power-off-first table. Presented as normal practice, not as failure.

safety.description: Kept structurally separate from every child-facing section.

mode.description: No value means 'powered and released'. A lab cannot declare a live circuit.

power_profile.description: Required whenever mode is not 'unpowered'. Every value comes from verified evidence; a guessed value is not allowed.

visuals.description: Dual coding (Paivio; Mayer): every visual is tied to the section it supports, so words and pictures are processed together rather than competing. Exact electronic fact comes only from verified photographs or deterministic renders.

placement_steps.description: Numbered, matching the written steps one-to-one — spatial contiguity, so the child never holds two orderings in mind.

unpowered_path_map.description: Foundation-lab replacement for the breadboard map. States what the child can see, point to, trace or record while everything is disconnected. Never imitates a powered build.

source_kind.description: verified_photograph and deterministic_render may carry exact electronic fact. imagegen may not — it is limited to context, mechanism illustration, observation support and polish.

supports_section.description: Dual coding requires the visual to sit with the text it explains, not float free.
